mechanism_narrative: A surge in housing starts (HOUST) above 1400 units, indicating strengthening demand, boosts consumer confidence, leading to increased spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:historical correlation between HOUST and consumer confidence
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 50% of instances when HOUST > 1400, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 4.5% signals accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as investors seek higher yields in equities.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns when FEDFUNDS < 4.5% are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) drops below 4.0%, signaling a tight labor market, and payroll employment (PAYEMS) grows by more than 200,000 in the previous month, the combined effect predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, due to increased consumer spending and business investment.
evidence_refs: fact:historical labor market indicators and stock market performance
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of instances when both conditions are met, or Rank IC < 0.01 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a quarter, indicating strengthening supply chains, predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as improved productivity boosts corporate earnings.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns when INDPRO growth > 2% are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the GDP annualized growth rate (GDPC1) below 2%, signaling weakening demand, predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, as reduced consumer and business spending impacts corporate earnings.
evidence_refs: fact:historical GDP growth and stock market performance
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 50% of instances when GDPC1 growth < 2%, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5.5% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) growth is above 3% in the previous quarter, the combined effect predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, due to reduced consumer spending and increased borrowing costs.
evidence_refs: fact:historical monetary policy and inflation indicators
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 40% of instances when both conditions are met, or Rank IC < 0.01 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5pp in two consecutive months, signaling labor market weakness, predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending.
evidence_refs: fact:historical labor market indicators and short-term stock market reactions
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 5-day forward returns when UNRATE increases > 0.5pp are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Always-on signal: the level of retail and food services sales (RSAFS) consistently predicts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as this indicator reflects the overall health of the US consumer.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns are not significantly correlated with RSAFS levels (t-test p > 0.05).
